blockedApps.name: DealCloud
blockedApps.blocker: Requires being an existing paying DealCloud client with admin-provisioned API access; no self-serve trial/sandbox account discoverable, no MCP server (official or community) found.

blockedApps.name: Gladly
blockedApps.blocker: No public self-serve trial/signup (enterprise sales-led, ~$20-30k/yr contracts); API token creation additionally requires admin-provisioned account role; no MCP server found (official or community).

blockedApps.name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
blockedApps.blocker: Requires an existing paid Commerce Cloud license/customer relationship (or ISV partner status) plus purchased sandbox credits to get API credentials — no public self-serve signup.

blockedApps.name: fanbasis
blockedApps.blocker: Could not access real endpoint/auth documentation: the main docs portal requires a login password, and the company/domain appears to be mid-rebrand from FanBasis to Commas, muddying which docs are current and public.

blockedApps.name: Clay
blockedApps.blocker: No general-purpose public API for an AI agent to call into Clay (create/read/update tables, trigger enrichments programmatically) was found — only inbound webhooks and workspace API keys scoped to specific in-platform actions; no official or community MCP server surfaced.

blockedApps.name: Paygent Connect
blockedApps.blocker: No discoverable public documentation, developer portal, or API reference for 'Paygent Connect' under that name — cannot confirm auth model, endpoints, or self-serve access.

blockedApps.name: PitchBook
blockedApps.blocker: No self-serve signup or public API reference; requires an existing paid PitchBook subscription plus a separate enterprise API contract and manual provisioning by PitchBook's Direct Data team.

blockedApps.name: NotebookLM
blockedApps.blocker: No self-serve API for consumer NotebookLM; the only documented API (Gemini Notebook Enterprise) requires a Google Cloud Enterprise agreement and is still Pre-GA/Preview.

blockedApps.name: Otter AI
blockedApps.blocker: Public API and official MCP server require an Enterprise plan plus manual account-manager enablement; no free/self-serve API key path.

blockedApps.name: Consensus
blockedApps.blocker: No public self-serve API key; both the REST API and the MCP server require being an existing paid/Enterprise Consensus customer.

partialApps.name: Podio
partialApps.blocker: Low default rate limit (250 req/hr per client_id) constrains agent workloads; no MCP server found (official or community).

partialApps.name: Zendesk
partialApps.blocker: No official MCP server yet (announced, not shipped); community MCP servers exist as a workaround.

partialApps.name: Freshdesk
partialApps.blocker: Official MCP integration is Beta/EAP and reportedly restricted to Enterprise-plan customers; direct REST API itself is fully buildable today.

partialApps.name: WhatsApp Business
partialApps.blocker: Real production sending (beyond the sandbox test number/24h session window) requires Meta Business verification and, for marketing messages, template approval.

partialApps.name: Aircall
partialApps.blocker: API/OAuth credential access is gated behind a paid Professional-tier-or-higher plan and, for OAuth apps, a manual request to Aircall for client credentials — not a free/instant self-serve signup.

partialApps.name: Google Ads
partialApps.blocker: Developer token defaults to test-account-only access; production-account use requires a manual Google review/approval process before real campaigns can be managed.

partialApps.name: Meta Ads
partialApps.blocker: Sensitive/advanced permissions require Meta App Review and business verification before an agent can act on a live ad account beyond low-volume/dev-mode limits.

partialApps.name: LinkedIn Ads
partialApps.blocker: Full production access gated behind LinkedIn's manual application review (up to 30 business days) tied to a specific declared use case.

partialApps.name: systeme.io
partialApps.blocker: API surface is documented narrowly (mainly contacts/tags); full funnel/course/product management coverage is unclear from public docs, limiting what an agent could reliably automate beyond contact/CRM operations.

partialApps.name: Pinterest
partialApps.blocker: Trial-tier access (the easy, fast-approval tier) only produces sandboxed content invisible to real users; genuine production use requires a second manual Standard-access review with a video demo.

partialApps.name: Threads
partialApps.blocker: Production/public use requires Meta Tech Provider Verification and App Review for sensitive scopes; no Composio toolkit currently exists (confirmed absent from Composio's Social Media and Advertising & Marketing category listings) and no MCP server was found.

partialApps.name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
partialApps.blocker: Requires either self-hosting the free Magento Open Source edition yourself (no shared vendor sandbox) or a paid Adobe Commerce license for the managed/cloud edition.

partialApps.name: Amazon Selling Partner API
partialApps.blocker: Requires an approved Professional Seller Central account plus Amazon's Developer Profile review (and marketplace listing for public apps) before real API credentials are issued — not a same-day self-serve signup.

partialApps.name: Ahrefs
partialApps.blocker: Requires a paid Ahrefs subscription (Lite $129/mo+) to obtain an API key; no free-tier credentials for a developer to self-serve test with beyond the limited public Domain Rating endpoint.

partialApps.name: MrScraper
partialApps.blocker: Could not confirm free/self-serve trial credentials or full API reference from public docs in the time budgeted; docs.mrscraper.com content is thin/fragmented across proxy vs. scraper products.

partialApps.name: Sherlock
partialApps.blocker: No hosted API/service exists at all — any agent integration requires wrapping the local CLI (subprocess execution) rather than calling an endpoint, and there's no official MCP server, only community wrappers.

partialApps.name: Waterfall.io
partialApps.blocker: Could not verify signup/trial mechanics or pricing gate from public docs within budget — real documentation exists (docs.waterfall.io) but is thin on go-to-market details, and no MCP or Composio presence was found.

partialApps.name: Neo4j
partialApps.blocker: Aura management API requires billing info on file before API credentials can be issued on Free/Professional tiers; data-plane access is Cypher-over-Bolt rather than a conventional REST resource surface, so 'API surface' is narrow relative to other apps here.

partialApps.name: Plaid
partialApps.blocker: Sandbox is instantly self-serve, but real (production) bank-linked data requires Plaid's application/compliance approval process, and no official or community MCP server was found.

partialApps.name: Binance
partialApps.blocker: No official/community MCP server found; Composio has no dedicated Binance toolkit (only adjacent crypto tools like CoinMarketCap/Bitquery under its 'Crypto-Kit'), and full trading functionality requires KYC-gated account access.

partialApps.name: iPayX
partialApps.blocker: Vendor claims an official MCP server and REST API/SDKs directly on its marketing site, but the specific docs URL (ipayx.ai/docs) returned a 404, so the actual API reference could not be independently verified beyond the homepage's self-description.

partialApps.name: Devin
partialApps.blocker: Requires a paid Teams ($500/mo) or Enterprise Devin plan to obtain an API key; not accessible on the free/individual Core tier.

partialApps.name: Grain
partialApps.blocker: Requires being an existing Grain (paying customer/workspace member) account holder to issue a Personal or Workspace Access Token; no free/anonymous developer sandbox found.
